item.title: Conductance of silicon nanotube junctions in high magnetic fields
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Silicon nanotube junctions show irregular transmission oscillations without forming conductive gateway states under fields up to 60 T. Perpendicular magnetic field alters transmission significantly more than parallel field.

Grade 0.417 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “exchange gates and two-qubit operations in semiconductor double quantum dots” · Teresa Kulka, Juan Alberto Canché-Martín, Irina V. Lebedeva, Jacek A. Majewski, Karolina Z. Milowska

Figure

Electronic transmission of metallic (6,0)+(6,0) silicon nanotube junctions versus energy under perpendicular and parallel magnetic fields up to 60 T, showing irregular oscillations with overlap length and field orientation.

Asks

How do magnetic-field direction, field strength, overlap length, and inter-tube spacing affect coherent quantum transport in silicon nanotube junctions?

But

Tight-binding simulations neglecting the Zeeman contribution (g≈2, ∼7 meV splitting at 60 T). Coherent transport regime.

Tools

four-orbital tight-binding model · Peierls substitution · non-equilibrium Green's function formalism · DFT benchmarking (PBE-GGA)

Abstract

We investigate coherent quantum transport through silicon nanotube (SiNT) junctions in high magnetic fields up to 60 T using a tight-binding model combined with the non-equilibrium Green's function formalism, and magnetic field included via Peierls substitution. We consider junctions of metallic nanotubes (6,0)+(6,0) and semiconducting ones (9,9)+(9,9), and examine the effects of the overlap length, inter-tube distance, magnetic-field direction, and field strength on the electronic transmission. In contrast to carbon nanotube junctions, the SiNT systems exhibit irregular transmission oscillations and do not show the emergence of highly conductive gateway states. The transmission is substantially more sensitive to a magnetic field perpendicular to the nanotube axis than to a parallel field, while increasing the field strength progressively modifies the transmission spectrum. Increasing the overlap length results in more frequent transmission oscillations, whereas increasing the inter-tube distance modifies their positions and amplitudes without changing their overall character. Generally, similar trends are observed for both types of junctions, involving metallic and semiconducting nanotubes. However, in the junction of semiconducting nanotubes, one observes peculiar additional field-dependent in-gap transmission features. These results demonstrate that the magnetic-field response of SiNT junctions is strongly governed by their geometry and differs qualitatively from that of pristine carbon nanotube junctions.

item.title: The non-equilibrium condensate-like state in multi-mode driven dissipative superconducting quantum circuit
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Periodic flux tuning of an intermediate transmon selectively engages a dissipative transmon to reversibly switch a target fluxonium between a high-occupation non-equilibrium condensate-like state and a low-occupation state without changing intrinsic target loss.

Grade 0.403 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity quantum electrodynamics for superconducting electrical circuits: An arch…” · Jing Li, Chaoying Zhao

Figure

Target-fluxonium occupation, state deviations, and recovery metrics under noise injection into the intermediate transmon versus directly into the fluxonium as functions of operating detuning Δ1.

Asks

Can a driven non-equilibrium state in a superconducting circuit be temporarily depleted via an auxiliary dissipative channel and fully recovered without increasing intrinsic target-mode loss?

But

Numerical open-system simulations under rotating-wave approximation and nearest-neighbor coupling.

Tools

fluxonium-transmon-transmon (FTT) circuit · Lindblad master equation · periodic flux modulation · filter-function noise analysis

Abstract

The effective decay rate of traditional single mode model for an open quantum system can't accurately described the exchange between intermodes and dissipation caused by the environment,therefore we can not clearly see the occupation pathway of target mode or the transient participation of auxiliary modes.At the same time,we also can't address the selective dissipation pathways resulting from the circuit design.In order to solving above problem,we adopt fluxonium-transmon-transmon (FTT)-based three mode model to describe dynamical characteristics of dissipation spectrum in superconducting quantum circuits.In terms of periodic flux modulation,we find out the pathways of intermode occupation transfer and environmental release for the target fluxonium changes from a high occupation nonequilibrium condensate-like state to low occupation equilibrium Bose-Einstein condensation(BEC)state.Without increasing the intrinsic loss of the target mode in the process of adjusting the auxiliary mode,we furthermore obtain additional selectively engaged environmental dissipative pathway.Our model can provides a new design perspective for non-equilibrium state recovery in a controllable dissipation superconducting quantum circuit.

item.title: Quantum Gates Built on a Spin Qubit and a Kitaev Parity Qubit
item.description:
Long shot theory — Hybrid architecture couples a quantum-dot spin qubit to a Kitaev parity qubit via spin-dependent Majorana delocalization, enabling parity qubit readout fidelity >98%, iSWAP gate fidelity of 90% (compensable to 98%), and CZ gate fidelity of 99%.

Grade 0.399 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “exchange gates and two-qubit operations in semiconductor double quantum dots” · Zhi-Hai Liu, Jiang Zhang, Guilu Long, H. Q. Xu

Figure

Gate schemes and operational dynamics for single-qubit rotations, readout probabilities Pσ±(t), and iSWAP gate matrix elements Kjj′ with corresponding phase distributions between the spin qubit and Kitaev parity qubit.

Asks

How does the nonlocal spin structure of poor-man's Majorana modes govern the interaction between a Kitaev parity qubit and a spin qubit in semiconductor-superconductor quantum dot arrays?

But

Theoretical simulation assuming strong intradot Coulomb repulsion on Q0, finite Zeeman splitting bounded by critical field, and idealized dynamical decoupling pulse sequences.

Tools

minimal Kitaev chains (MKCs) · electric-dipole spin resonance (EDSR) · dynamical decoupling (DD) · Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) modeling · semiconductor-superconductor hybrid quantum dots

Abstract

Spin is typically traced out in the description of quantum-dot-based Kitaev chains to simplify the construction of Majorana fermions. Yet the intrinsic spin structure of poor-man's Majorana modes in minimal Kitaev chains under finite Zeeman fields offers a natural interface for the Kitaev parity qubit to interact with other spinful systems. Here, we establish such a platform to bridge the parity qubit and a quantum-dot spin qubit, with the effective coupling governed by the spin-dependent delocalization of the Majorana modes. Depending on whether the spin qubit is coupled to one or two chains constituting the parity qubit, the parity-spin coupling exhibits distinct forms: an anisotropic parity-conserving exchange interaction or a nontrivial exchange tensor tunable via the interchain superconducting-phase bias. Leveraging fast spin-qubit manipulation, we further demonstrate universal parity-qubit control, high-fidelity qubit-state readout, and entangling operations between the parity and spin qubits. These results turn the spinful structure of poor-man's Majoranas from a finite-field imperfection into a resource for hybrid quantum control.
